title: Afraid of flying
summary: Pilar is terrified of planes, but her best friend's wedding is in Canada.
paragraphs: Pilar had never been on a plane. She was not afraid of spiders, the dark or high places, but planes {{terrified}} her. When she saw one in the sky, she felt her heart beat faster. So when her best friend Rocío told her that her wedding would be in Canada, Pilar was happy for her and also very, very worried.

She thought about all the other ways to get there. A boat would take more than a week. There was no train across the ocean. She had to fly. "Eight hours," she said to herself every night. "Eight hours in the air." She read about plane {{accidents}} online, which made everything worse.

Her doctor recommended a course for people who are afraid of flying. Pilar was surprised to find twelve other people in the room, all of them nervous like her. A pilot explained how planes work, why they don't fall and what the strange noises mean. "{{Turbulence}} is like a bus on a bumpy road," he said. "Uncomfortable, but not dangerous." They practised {{breathing}} exercises and, on the last day, they sat in a real plane on the ground.

On the day of the flight, Pilar was shaking. She told the flight attendant that she was afraid, and the attendant smiled and checked on her every hour. When the plane took off, Pilar closed her eyes and held the seat very tightly. After twenty minutes she opened them. Below the window, the clouds looked like a white field of snow, shining in the sun.

She was still nervous for most of the flight, but she watched two films, ate a terrible sandwich and even slept for an hour. At the wedding, Rocío hugged her and said, "I can't believe you came!" Pilar laughed. "Neither can I," she said. On the way home, she asked for a {{window}} seat.

accidents.meaning: bad events that happen by chance and hurt people or damage things

breathing.meaning: taking air into your body and letting it out

window.meaning: an opening in a wall or vehicle with glass, so you can see out

turbulence.meaning: sudden movements of air that make a plane shake

questions.question: Why did Pilar have to fly?
options: She wanted to visit a friend on holiday.
Her best friend's wedding was in Canada.
She had a job interview abroad.
questions.explanation: Rocío's wedding was in Canada, and there was no other good way to get there.

questions.question: What made her fear worse?
questions.explanation: She read about plane accidents online, which made everything worse.

questions.question: How did the pilot describe turbulence?
options: Like a bus on a bumpy road
Like a boat in a storm
questions.explanation: He said turbulence is like a bus on a bumpy road: uncomfortable but not dangerous.

questions.question: What shows that Pilar felt better on the way home?
options: She slept for the whole flight.
She asked for a window seat.
She sat next to the pilot.
questions.explanation: On the way home, she asked for a window seat.
